items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: he moved in with the family of Lawrence’s brother, Harold Brown.

ctx.x: Oh, it was so romantic. So while I was doing all this, somebody showed up with a vase with roses and put it on the lectern or whatever you call it, the pulpit. I said, “roses, this is like Rudolph Valentino.” And it was some woman’s name signed to the roses, I have no idea who it was, and so that was that. Bobby Short was a little boy who was a kiddie performer. And when he went out to California he moved in with you know, little colored kids, or any kids on the road I guess had trouble finding accommodations.…
You just started to touch on a subject that I find interesting and that is the racial thing that was happening at that time, with this music and the fans, and how did that kind of balance —
